name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain ui_menu, descriptor screen_sprite_atlas_buf_ptr. Accurately reflects both the role (sprite atlas buffer for the chapter-intro/menu screens) and the data type (uint32 holding a heap pointer; '_buf_ptr' suffix). No Ghidra address residue in the name. DATATYPE in Ghidra is undefined4; symbol name matches live Ghidra byte-identical.
purpose: Heap-pointer global to the on-demand FDOTHER.DAT sprite atlas buffer used by the chapter-intro / menu screens (the BG-image + dialog/money-panel sprite source).
logic_summary: Owner flows (fd2_main_menu_continue_dispatcher, fd2_chapter_transition_menu, fd2_run_chapter_intro_menu_main/typeB/typeC) malloc the buffer via fd2_load_dat_resource(FDOTHER, <prev ptr>, entry), store the returned pointer here, use it as the atlas base, then free() it and write 0 back. The FDOTHER entry index varies by screen: CONTINUE dispatcher and chapter-transition menu use 0x0D (verified PUSH 0xd at 0x25f48 and 0x2cca0); chapter-intro _main uses 0x0C/0x1D/0x3F by cursor state, typeB 0x0D, typeC 0x0E. Many render helpers read it as the atlas base and add the sprite-record offset-table entry at +0x0E (e.g. fd2_blit_money_digit_sprite at 0x2d636: MOV EBX,[0x54147]; ADD EBX,[EBX+0x0E]).
datatype: uint32 (4 bytes; holds a heap pointer / void*)
element_semantics: Scalar pointer value: address of the malloc'd FDOTHER sprite atlas buffer, or 0 when not loaded. Atlas layout has a sprite-record offset table at byte +0x0E used by the blit helpers.
comment_original_issue: The source comment block was accurate and detailed but over-narrowed the load to 'FDOTHER.DAT entry 0x0D' as if it were the only entry; the three chapter-intro menus in the same file reuse this pointer with other entries (0x0C/0x1D/0x3F/0x0E).
notes: Memory at 0x54147 reads 16 zero bytes (BSS, load-time zeroed). Write xrefs from the game confirm mutable runtime state -> not const. No existing Ghidra data plate (PLATE was <none>); created a concise src-derived plate via run_script_inline + setComment(PLATE_COMMENT). Source comment edited via Edit (one block only); other symbols' comments in the file untouched.
